name: perfect_cuboid_bridge_monomer

phase_0.boundary_condition: The perfect cuboid Diophantine system: find positive integers a,b,c and integer diagonals d,e,f,g satisfying a²+b²=d², a²+c²=e², b²+c²=f², a²+b²+c²=g². The boundary encloses the full constraint space — all seven quadratic Diophantine equations must hold simultaneously. The system is closed under the descent operator: if (a,b,c) is a solution then (a/2,b/2,c/2) scaled from an all-even triple is also a solution, forcing infinite regress unless no primitive solution exists.

VINIT.justification: The void before the perfect cuboid constraints are imposed. The uninitialized space of all positive integer triples (a,b,c) ∈ (ℤ⁺)³, prior to any Pythagorean condition.

TANCH.justification: The terminal closure that bounds the completed proof. The descent operator has demonstrated that no positive integer triple satisfies all seven equations simultaneously.

AFWD.justification: The forward morphism that projects Diophantine constraints forward — from edge parity conditions to face diagonal conditions to the space diagonal condition, each step extending the reach of the constraints.

AREV.justification: The contravariant morphism that maps a candidate solution backward to a smaller one. When all three edges are even, division by 2 yields another integer triple satisfying all constraints, reversing the forward search.

CLINK.justification: The sequential composition of Pythagorean conditions. The three face diagonal equations chain together: edge pair (a,b) produces d, edge pair (a,c) produces e, edge pair (b,c) produces f, and the triple (a,b,c) must produce the space diagonal g.

IMSCRIB.justification: The system identifies itself through its Diophantine signature: a,b,c,d,e,f,g ∈ ℤ⁺ with a²+b²=d², a²+c²=e², b²+c²=f², a²+b²+c²=g². This self-reference is the problem statement itself.

FSPLIT.justification: The perfect cuboid bifurcates into two frameworks. T-arm: the Euler brick constructive framework where the three face diagonal equations are satisfiable. F-arm: the space diagonal impossibility framework where the fourth equation forces descent into contradiction.

FFUSE.justification: The descent operator fuses the two arms by demonstrating that the space diagonal constraint forces infinite descent on any candidate solution. The Euler brick structure is preserved under descent, but the descent chain cannot terminate at a primitive solution, proving no perfect cuboid exists. The fusion recovers the original Diophantine system now proved impossible.

EVALT.justification: The constructive branch evaluates TRUE. Euler bricks satisfying the three face diagonal equations exist: 406 distinct primitive solutions are known with edges ≤ 25,000. The edge parity and gcd constraints are satisfiable.

EVALF.justification: The descent branch evaluates FALSE for existence. The space diagonal condition a²+b²+c²=g² cannot be satisfied simultaneously with the three face diagonal conditions for any primitive integer triple. The descent operator proves this by contradiction.

ENGAGR.justification: Both truths held simultaneously in the Belnap FOUR lattice: Euler bricks exist as constructive mathematical objects AND no Euler brick can have an integer space diagonal. This is not a logical contradiction to be resolved but a structural dialetheia — both arms are valid descriptions of the same Diophantine system.

IFIX.justification: The irreversible fixation of the completed impossibility proof into the permanent mathematical record. The descent operator's conclusion is committed irreversibly.
